Schedule technical benchmark (30-60 minute) with Empiric infra team w/ sample workload - target week of 2026-03-16
Share SOC2 + network diagram and KMS docs

Samir Patel - prep benchmark config template and sample load script for Empiric - due 2026-03-12

meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-05 | Time: 11:00 AM - 11:38 AM ET | Duration: 38 mins | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Empiric Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Empiric CTO), Jenna Ortiz (Empiric Infra), Ethan Park (Empiric Product)
summary: Empiric Ventures is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and dedicated inference. Primary focus: per-token unit economics, batching and KV/prefix caching levers, and budget constraints for production recommender/chat features. Customer wants a clear cost model and a short benchmark to compare Redwood hosted pricing vs their projected self-hosted spend. Security and VPC options were raised but deferred to a follow-up security doc review.
topics: Introductions; current infra + usage patterns; cost model walkthrough (per-token pricing, embeddings); batching & prefix/KV cache effects; Dedicated reserved capacity and pricing; Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs (latency, cost, SLAs); next steps & benchmarking plan
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, really appreciate you taking the time. quick intro: with me are Samir and Lina from our SE team.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi all, Priya here, head of ml at Empiric. We're trying to understand the cost tradeoffs between your hosted offering and maybe reserved/dedicated capacity.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus, CTO. We're budget constrained this quarter, so unit economics are top of mind.
[00:26] Jenna Ortiz: Jenna infra, i'll be running the bench with you if we do a POC.
[00:30] Alex Morgan: Great. quick agenda: what you're running today, the features, target SLOs, then we walk through per-token pricing and batching/cache levers and then next steps. sound good?
[00:40] Ethan Park: Yep, thanks.
[00:45] Samir Patel: cool, i'll jump in on the technical bits. can you share current qps and typical request sizes?
[00:52] Priya Kapoor: Sure. For the recommender microservice, baseline is ~120 QPS peak, avg prompt token length is 80 tokens in, 40 tokens out on average; embeddings pipeline is batch of ~5k docs nightly, but realtime vector queries are about 150/sec.
[01:10] Samir Patel: nice, that helps. so roughing out, with hosted per-token pricing we model per-input + per-output tokens. for high qps with 80/40, the total token volume is... (mumbling) around X. one lever that helps a lot is batching for embeddings and prefix caching for chat/recs.
[01:32] Marcus Lee: quick question — your hosted per-token rates, do they include a discount for caching or is that charged same?
[01:40] Alex Morgan: hosted billing is per-token consumed from generation and embedding calls. caching and batching reduce tokens you have to generate which reduces cost; we don't bill separately for cache hits. so if you can prefix cache or use KV cache to avoid generating initial prefix, that's pure savings on your side.
[01:58] Priya Kapoor: ok, good. what's the typical hit-rate you'd expect for prefix caching on recs?
[02:05] Lina Cho: typical prefix cache hit rates depend on traffic locality. for personalized recs with stable context, hit rates of 30-60% are achievable. in a lot of customer workloads we see easy 25-35% on first pass, and then with tuned keys you can get higher.
[02:25] Jenna Ortiz: for our infra, we can probably shard cache by user bucket, get decent locality.
[02:30] Samir Patel: another lever is batching — for embeddings nightly we recommend batching to maximize throughput and use dedicated pools if you want predictable cost. for hosted, we can do autoscaling but latency during spikes can vary.
[02:45] Marcus Lee: Can you quantify the cost delta between hosted and Dedicated for steady high throughput?
[02:51] Alex Morgan: generally, hosted is great for bursty/low-to-mid steady usage. Dedicated reserved capacity moves you to a commitment model: monthly commit for GPUs which lowers per-token compute cost — typically 20-40% lower unit cost for large sustained usage, but you trade commit and some ops work. exact numbers depend on model size, seq length, and batching. we'll send a tailored comparison.
[03:16] Priya Kapoor: what about quantization/accelerators — do those affect pricing?
[03:21] Samir Patel: yes, we support quantized variants which reduce GPU memory and improve throughput; that changes kernel selection and can lower cost per token. For hosted we have Redwood-verified quantized models; on Dedicated you can pin quantization/variants. Pricing adjustments reflect the compute profile; we'll include those scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[03:40] Ethan Park: we also care about latency tail SLOs. dedicated pools can offer tighter latency. do you have numbers?
[03:47] Lina Cho: SLA targets for Dedicated are tighter, we can commit to p99 under certain loads. Hosted has published latency profiles per model; for small models p50 is low, p99 depends on concurrency and queueing. we'll share benchmarks.
[04:05] Marcus Lee: curious about autoscaling — if we have a sudden spike, does Dedicated allow bursting?
[04:11] Alex Morgan: yes, Dedicated has burst capacity options or short-term autoscale to shared pools. you can configure policies to prefer dedicated first then fallback to hosted variants; that helps maintain SLOs.
[04:22] Priya Kapoor: ok, let's talk numbers. walk me through a simplified per-request cost calc.
[04:27] Samir Patel: simple example: assume hosted rate $0.0006 per input token and $0.0012 per output token for a model profile — with 80/40 tokens that's ~0.0006*80 + 0.0012*40 = 0.048 + 0.048 = $0.096 per request. at 120 QPS sustained that's quite large monthly. but prefix caching with a 40% hit rate reduces generated tokens significantly — effective cost drops by similar percent. embeddings are typically priced differently e.g., $0.0002 per vector or per 1k tokens — we'll give exact.
[05:10] Marcus Lee: those per-token numbers seem high vs some public list prices — are those bundled for managed infra?
[05:16] Alex Morgan: yes, hosted includes managed infra, autoscaling, DDoS protections, monitoring and support. raw self-host on spot instances may look cheaper but you need to factor ops cost, reliability risk, and quality regressions. Dedicated reserved capacity narrows that gap.
[05:36] Jenna Ortiz: on the dedicated sizing, do you have a quick thumb rule for how many GPUs we'd need for 120 QPS with that seq length?
[05:44] Samir Patel: depends on model variant, quantization and batching. as a ballpark, for a 7B-like model quantized with batching and aggressive KV cache we might need 2-3 A100-equivalent GPUs for sustained 120 QPS if you shard and use batching. for larger models it's more. we'll propose a specific dedicated sizing.
[06:05] Priya Kapoor: can we run a short benchmark? we want sample p50/p90/p99 and cost metrics per 24h ramp.
[06:12] Alex Morgan: absolutely. typical benchmark is 2 phases: an initial correctness/latency run with your sample prompts and then a 24h load run. we can run this on hosted for quick results or if you want dedicated-level numbers we can spin up a dedicated trial env. Jenna, which would you prefer?
[06:28] Jenna Ortiz: I'd prefer hosted first to validate correctness & cost, then a dedicated trial if numbers look promising.
[06:34] Marcus Lee: agree. can you also include a comparison against our internal self-host cost model? we run models on spot and also have some ml infra costs.
[06:42] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll provide a side-by-side: hosted unit price, dedicated amortized unit price with commit, and an estimate for self-host including ops overhead.
[06:51] Priya Kapoor: security - we need SSO, audit logs and maybe KMS. how does Redwood handle that?
[06:58] Lina Cho: Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and for Private/Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. Hosted can use our managed KMS but we also offer bring-your-own-key on higher tiers. we'll share SOC2 + network diagrams.
[07:15] Ethan Park: good. Data retention and tenancy? we need strict controls for some PII.
[07:20] Samir Patel: Dedicated gives you isolation at the pool level and options for data retention policies. Private deployments can be VPC or on-prem for strict regs.
[07:29] Marcus Lee: any gotchas on model fallbacks? like if dedicated is at capacity and we fallback to hosted variant, does that change latency or model behavior?
[07:36] Alex Morgan: yes, fallback can go to a compatible variant — behavior may differ slightly if it's a quantized or smaller model; we surface compatibility matrices and let you pin policies. fallback is meant for availability not for A/B testing; you should plan for regression testing.
[07:51] Priya Kapoor: ok, thanks. can we get a sample cost calc for embeddings? we do nightly embeddings of 5k docs and realtime vector queries at 150/sec.
[07:59] Samir Patel: embeddings: if hosted price is e.g., $0.0003 per 1k tokens or $0.0004 per vector (varies by model), nightly cost for 5k docs at average tokens per doc will be small relative to realtime query cost. Real-time vector index queries cost is mostly about serving infrastructure per qps, and Dedicated index nodes can be cheaper per query. we'll put numbers in sheet.
[08:24] Jenna Ortiz: we have an existing vector DB billed separately; how do we integrate?
[08:29] Lina Cho: we support integration with your vector DB, or you can use our managed indexes. if you keep your DB, only embeddings and retrieval calls route through Redwood and costs reflect those calls.
[08:41] Marcus Lee: okay, timeline wise, we want to decide by end of month. what's typical POC duration?
[08:46] Alex Morgan: most POCs are 2-4 weeks; for a dedicated trial we do a short pilot 4-6 weeks. we'll tailor to your decision timeline.
[08:55] Priya Kapoor: final clarifying Q - for hosted, is there a committed discount if we reach >X tokens/month?
[09:02] Alex Morgan: we have tiered volume discounts and enterprise committed usage discounts. if you hit sustained volumes we can move to reserved/dedicated pricing or enterprise tier with better rates.
[09:11] Ethan Park: any reference customers in fintech or adtech who did similar migration?
[09:16] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll share anonymous case studies and a benchmark summary — examples include companies running high-qps recommenders.
[09:24] Samir Patel: ok, summarizing next steps: we'll send pricing + cost model, plan a hosted benchmark run with sample prompts, and provide SOC2 & KMS docs. Jenna will share traffic profile and sample prompts.
[09:37] Jenna Ortiz: I'll send sample payloads and 7 days of telemetry by Monday.
[09:42] Alex Morgan: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the benchmark.
[09:48] Priya Kapoor: thanks all.
[09:50] [call ends]
